# TLS trust anchor
Adds a **Certificate trust** section to DeepSeek Harness Settings where a host can be marked to skip
TLS certificate verification — so a private model gateway behind a self-signed certificate connects
instead of failing with `Connection error`.

[](https://www.npmjs.com/package/dsh-tls-trust-anchor)[](https://github.com/spark-ai-boy/dsh-tls-tru

## The problem
Node.js verifies TLS with its **own** CA store. It never reads the macOS or Windows system trust sto
re, so a certificate that Safari, Chrome, or a Bun-based CLI accepts can still be rejected inside th
te that Safari, Chrome, or a Bun-based CLI accepts can still be rejected inside the Harness runtime:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
A self-signed leaf certificate (`Basic Constraints: CA:FALSE`) cannot act as a trust anchor at all u
nless OpenSSL is told to accept a partial chain, and Node does not expose that switch through a prov
ider configuration. There is no provider-level certificate or trust option to set.
## What it does
- **Per-host switch** — add `newapi.example.com`, decide whether to skip verification for it, remove

it again. The decision applies to that host only.
- **Only that host** — no certificate store edits
, no other application affected. Every other connection keeps standard verification: expiry, unknown

roots, and hostname mismatches are all still rejected.
- **Child processes too** — while the plugin
is active it appends a `--require` preload to `NODE_OPTIONS`, so Node children the Harness spawns (

a model gateway proxy that runs on its own, for example) follow the same per-host policy.
- **Persis

ted** — the list lives in `~/.dsh/tls-trust/trusted-hosts.json` and survives restarts.
- **Live** —
the Host patches `tls.connect` for the Harness runtime; the switch takes effect on the next request,
ls.connect` for the Harness runtime; the switch takes effect on the next request, without a restart.
## Install
### Requirements

- DeepSeek Harness 0.2.x desktop or web profile, with third-party plugin installation enabled
- The
model endpoint you want to trust
### Source
The Harness plugin manager installs from a GitHub repository or an npm package:

- **GitHub repository**: `https://github.com/spark-ai-boy/dsh-tls-trust-anchor`
- **npm package**: `
dsh-tls-trust-anchor`
### Steps

1. Open **Settings → Plugins**, install the bundle from the repository or npm.
2. Open **Settings →
Models** and add your provider with its `baseURL`, API type, and key. The `baseURL` is the API root,
so enter `https://newapi.example.com` — not `https://newapi.example.com/v1`, because the client app

ends `/v1/messages` itself.
3. Open **Settings → Certificate trust**, type the hostname, and press *

*Add host**. The switch defaults to on (verification skipped).
4. Return to the chat and select the

ost**. The switch defaults to on (verification skipped).
4. Return to the chat and select the model.
## Security
Skipping verification keeps the connection **encrypted** but stops proving **who the peer is**. Use
it only for a certificate you control, and prefer a properly issued certificate whenever one is avai
lable. The trust list is narrow by design: a version check, an expired certificate, or an unknown ro
ot on any other host is still refused.
Removing a host from the list immediately restores standard verification for it on the next request.
## How it works
| Half | Behaviour |
| Host (`index.js`) | Reads the persisted list, patches `tls.connect` inside the Harness runtime, an

d serves the `tlsTrust` Remote service |
| Client (`client.js`) | Registers a `settings.section` row

and renders the list, switch, and delete button |
| State (`src/host/state.js`) | Hostname normalis

ation and JSON persistence |
| Preload (`src/host/preload.cjs`) | Enters child processes through `NO
DE_OPTIONS=--require`, reads the same list, and patches per host |
Only connections whose `servername`/`host` matches a trusted entry get `rejectUnauthorized: false`.
Everything else is passed through untouched.
## Limitations
- The Host half imports `@deepseek-ai/dsh-typert-protocol`, which the Harness installation provides.

It is not bundled.
- Remote method parameter names are read from Host source when no generated Type
rt artifact is present, so the names in `client.js` descriptors must match the Host method signature

s verbatim.
- A child process only inherits the policy if it starts **after** the plugin activated;
a long-running process that predates it needs one restart.
